reason: The observation is correct and the fix is wrong, and the consequence is overstated on two counts. Correct: driven in chromium at 1440 across full, partial and first-run, the four status cards paint 'haven't moved in a fortnight' / 'past the day they were due' / 'has nobody's name on it' / 'are waiting on something else', and the group names read '3 jobs haven't moved in a fortnight, of 9 jobs open' beside '2 jobs past the day they were due, of 9 jobs open'. The measurement also checks out: substituting 'are past the day they were due' into the .t-small at 390/768/1280/1440 leaves the small block at 40.28/20.14/40.28/40.28px, one line, and the card at 156.64/136.50/156.64/156.64px — identical to the pixel. Where it fails: (1) The plural string is load-bearing in a second construction the seat did not read. word.many is spliced, without a count, into the unavailable branch at lately.html:730 ('Jobs ${word.many}: not available, because Timeline did not answer') and rendered as the visible small text at :736 — and the overdue card is the ONLY card that ever passes unavailable:true (:866, state=partial). Driven at ?state=partial, that card today paints '— / past the day they were due / NOT AVAILABLE' and speaks 'Jobs past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer'. Apply the proposed one-line edit verbatim and it becomes 'Jobs are past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer' — a bare assertion of the exact fact the card exists to say it does not hold, immediately contradicted by its own clause. That is a regression on a protected object (the honest-degradation contract), and interaction-check.mjs will not catch it: the only assertions touching that string are naSaysWords and srSaysWhy at :295 and :298, both /not available/i, both still green. A fix that silently degrades a protected state past a gate that cannot see it is a worse trade than the fragment it removes. (2) The 'four-item parallel' premise is a scoped quotation. The row is five cards — the band's own label says 'All five counted out of 9' — and the fifth, the lead denominator card, paints 'jobs not finished' in the same .kpi, same .t-small slot: a bare noun phrase, by design. The row already contains a non-finite label, so the overdue card is the second of five, not the one break in four. (3) The claim that 'one card changes grammatical class with its own count' is a code path no shipped state reaches. word.one fires only at overdue === 1, and every scope in fixture.js is full 2, quiet 0, first-run 0, partial unavailable — confirmed by driving all four: the singular never painted once. A class change nobody can observe is not a defect. Severity corrected from defect to refinement: nothing on screen is untrue, nothing is broken, and what remains is a label that reads as a noun phrase rather than a clause in one of five cards. The corrected fix is in sharpenedFix and is worth taking only if the partial branch is separated first.
sharpenedFix: Do not edit lately.html:866 alone. Separate the two jobs the plural string is doing, then change the visible one. In kpi() at lately.html:724, take an optional naPhrase defaulting to word.many; at :730 build the unavailable name as `Jobs ${naPhrase}: not available, because Timeline did not answer`; at :736 render `known ? phrase : naPhrase`. Then at :866 set many: "are past the day they were due" and naPhrase: "past the day they were due". The partial state keeps the noun phrase that construction requires and the full state gains the finite verb. Leave the lead card's 'jobs not finished' as it is — it is the denominator, not a status, and giving it a verb would make it assert a category it does not have.
breaks: As proposed (the bare :866 edit) it breaks the partial state's overdue card in both channels — visible text and the group's accessible name — turning a statement of unavailability into an assertion of overdue work followed by a denial of it, with both interaction-check.mjs assertions on that string (:295 naSaysWords, :298 srSaysWhy) still passing. If the sharpened form is taken instead, re-measure: .kpi heights and .t-small line counts at 390/768/1280/1440 in state=partial specifically, where the na branch's small block is 28px rather than 40px and sits above an extra 'Not available' label, so it has less slack than the full-state block I measured; the full-state group names in both grounds; and add an assertion to interaction-check.mjs that the unavailable card's aria-label does not open with a finite claim about the category — that is the guard whose absence let this fix look free.
